name: Iraqi Arabic (Baghdad / gilit)

ancestors.notes: Persian adstrate: extensive loanwords; /p/, /v/, /tʃ/, /ʒ/ phonemes; some phonological calques

notes: Iraqi Arabic — Baghdad Muslim / southern 'gilit' variety (the sedentary koine of Muslim Baghdad, Bedouin-type in origin). The gilit/qeltu split is the defining Mesopotamian isogloss, named after the reflex of the word 'I said': Muslim Baghdad gilit vs Mosul/Jewish/Christian qeltu (Blanc 1964, §2, §3.26). MODELLED FEATURES (cited): (1) DEFINING GILIT REFLEX — OA qaf ق → /ɡ/ (voiced velar; Bedouin origin): JC/qal/ vs M/gal/ 'to say' (Blanc 1964, §3.26, p.26–27; Jasim 2020, §2.4). MSA-learned words keep /q/ (e.g. القرآن), not orthographically separable. (2) GILIT KAF AFFRICATION — kaf ك → [tʃ] in a front-vowel environment (M/čan/ vs JC/kan/ 'he was'; M/čebir/ 'big'), modelled as allophone_rules IQ_GILIT_AFFRIC_K_* conditioned on an adjacent front vowel (Blanc 1964, §3.25, p.25; Jasim 2020, §2.9.2 — /tʃ/ is both a phoneme and an allophone of /k/ in gilit). ENGINE LIMIT: the fully LEXICALISED gilit affrication (M/čalb/ 'dog', where the trigger front vowel is historical) is not orthographically predictable and is NOT captured. LOAN-CLASS EXEMPTION: European loanwords stand OUTSIDE the lexicalized affrication class and keep plain [k] even before a high front vowel — كِيلُو 'kilo' → [kiːluː], not *[tʃiːluː] (Blanc 1964, §3.25: affrication is a historically lexicalized process, not a live rule reaching new loans; blind-judge consensus on the arbitrated gold). Since the affrication is expressed as a context rule that cannot tell a loan from an inherited stem, the exemption is carried as a word_exceptions entry. (3) qaf-reflex /ɡ/ → [dʒ] affrication before a front vowel (M/geʕad/ ~ [dʒeʕad] 'he sat'), allophone_rules IQ_GILIT_AFFRIC_G_* (Blanc 1964, §3.26 p.28; more regular in rural/Bedouin speech than urban Muslim Baghdad — lexically restricted). (4) INTERDENTALS PRESERVED — ث /θ/, ذ /ð/, ظ /ðˤ/ retained (conservative Mesopotamian feature; Blanc 1964, §3.2; Jasim 2020, §2.4) — unlike Levantine/Egyptian urban merger to /t d/. (5) jim ج → /dʒ/ (retained; inherited from ar-x-mashriqi). (6) EMPHATIC BACKING — low vowels /a aː/ → [ɑ ɑː] adjacent to an emphatic (tafxim; Jasim 2020, the thesis topic), allophone_rules IQ_EMPH_*. Persian adstrate: /p/, /v/, /tʃ/, /ʒ/ established as phonemes; thousands of Persian (and Ottoman-Turkish) loanwords (Blanc 1964, ch.6). INPUT CONTRACT: dialectal Arabic is normally written defectively; short vowels surface only when the input is vocalised (harakat). That is not a hypothetical for this spec's own benchmark row: not one of the 108 WikiPron acm_arab_broad input words carries a single haraka — no fatha, damma, kasra, tanwin, shadda or sukun occurs anywhere on the orthographic side — while the gold transcriptions are fully vocalised. Roughly a third of the gold's phoneme segments are therefore short vowels the input never supplies, and no grapheme table can recover them; docs/languages/ar.md tabulates the short-vowel share and the vowel-folded PER for this row alongside the other dialect rows. The remedy is a diacritized-input companion row, which exists for MSA (wikipron_ar_diacritized) and is registered for ar alone; wiring one here is the highest-value follow-up for this row, and it would have to be labelled restored-MSA input rather than native vocalisation, since the restorer targets MSA and Classical Arabic. Erwin (1963) A Short Reference Grammar of Iraqi Arabic is the standard descriptive grammar of gilit Baghdadi but was not obtainable (library/paywall) for this pass; features here are cited from Blanc 1964 and Jasim 2020, both read.

sources.notes: Read (OCR full text). §3.25 (p.25) OA/k/: in Muslim (gilit) split into /č/[tʃ] and /k/, JC preserve /k/ — M/čan/, JC/kan/ 'he was'; M/čebir/ 'big'. §3.26 (p.26–27) OA/q/: J and C reflex /q/ in practically every instance, M usually /g/ — JC/qal/, M/gal/ 'to say'; qaf-reflex /g/ affricates to [dʒ] before front vowels (p.28). §3.2 interdentals preserved in Muslim and Jewish. ch.6: Persian and Turkish loan strata; /p/ phoneme.

sources.author: Jasim, M.
sources.title: Tafxiːm in the vowels of Muslawi Qəltu and Baghdadi Gilit dialects of Arabic (PhD thesis)
sources.notes: Read (full PDF). §2.4: /q/ of Muslawi Qəltu is realised as voiced velar [ɡ] in Baghdadi Gilit — the defining split. §2.9.2: in Gilit /tʃ/ is both a separate phoneme and an allophone of /k/; in Muslawi Qəltu /k/ and /tʃ/ are separate phonemes with no allophony. Whole thesis documents tafxim (emphatic backing) of low vowels.

allophone_rules.notes: Gilit kaf affrication (Blanc 1964, §3.25 p.25; Jasim 2020, §2.9.2): /k/ → [tʃ] before an adjacent front vowel, e.g. M/čebir/ 'big'. The purely lexicalised residue (M/čan/, M/čalb/, where the trigger vowel is historical) is not orthographically predictable and is not captured.
Gilit kaf affrication (Blanc 1964, §3.25; Jasim 2020, §2.9.2): /k/ → [tʃ] after an adjacent front vowel.

Gilit qaf-reflex affrication (Blanc 1964, §3.26 p.28): the /ɡ/ reflex of OA qaf → [dʒ] before an adjacent front vowel, e.g. M/geʕad/ ~ [dʒeʕad] 'he sat'. Back-vowel words such as M/gal/ 'to say' (back /a/) do not fire, correctly. More regular in rural/Bedouin speech than in urban Muslim Baghdad; the lexicalised residue is not captured.
Gilit qaf-reflex affrication (Blanc 1964, §3.26): the /ɡ/ reflex of OA qaf → [dʒ] after an adjacent front vowel.
Emphatic backing / tafxim (Jasim 2020, the thesis topic; Blanc 1964, §3.3 — [ɑ] near emphatics): short /a/ → [ɑ] adjacent to an emphatic coronal.
Emphatic backing / tafxim (Jasim 2020; Blanc 1964, §3.3): short /a/ → [ɑ] after an emphatic coronal.
Emphatic backing / tafxim (Jasim 2020; Blanc 1964, §3.3): long /aː/ → [ɑː] adjacent to an emphatic coronal.
Emphatic backing / tafxim (Jasim 2020; Blanc 1964, §3.3): long /aː/ → [ɑː] after an emphatic coronal.

stress.notes: Arabic stress is QUANTITY-SENSITIVE: it falls on a syllable because that syllable is heavy, not because of any orthographic ending, so no ending table can express it. The cascade (Ryding, A Reference Grammar of MSA, CUP 2005, §2.3; Watson, The Phonology and Morphology of Arabic, OUP 2002, ch.3): a superheavy final syllable (CVːC/CVCC) takes the stress (kiˈtaːb); otherwise a heavy penult (CVː/CVC) does (muˈdarris); otherwise the antepenult (ˈmadrasa). max_onset=1 because Arabic onsets are obligatory and hold exactly one consonant — a medial cluster splits, closing the preceding syllable, and that boundary is what makes the penult of mudarris heavy. INPUT CONTRACT: weight is only recoverable from a complete transcription, so this requires diacritized input; an undiacritized skeleton has no vowels to weigh. The registered wikipron gold carries no stress marks, but the benchmark strips stress from both sides by default, so this costs no PER. Prosodic clitics: monosyllabic function words (negator maː, prepositions fiː/min/ʕan/ʕa/li/bi, vocative jaː, copula-negator muː/miʃ, conditional law/loː, wa-proclitic combinations) attach to a host and fall inside the host's stress domain, so they carry no word stress (Watson 2002, The Phonology and Morphology of Arabic, OUP, ch.3). Pan-Arabic class; the per-lect form list reflects the function words attested in this lect. Orthographic test — a clitic homograph (e.g. verb yā 'came') is destressed in every occurrence.

primary_sources.measured: The primary_sources row holds 12 gold pairs, per=0.2907, per_ci_low=0.176, per_ci_high=0.4065 (benchmarks/results.json). The 95% interval includes 0.25, so the row cannot be read as a failure. The same spec scores near zero on its other two rows (arabic_tts, n=20, per=0.0; gold20_arabic, n=20, per=0.0051), so Iraqi Arabic is not an unmeasured language overall -- only this thin gold set is.

wikipron.measured: 0 of 108 wikipron input words (acm_arab_broad.tsv) (scored under the 'acm' ISO 639-3 alias, which registry.py resolves to this spec) carry a haraka (short-vowel diacritic); Wiktionary files Arabic entries at the unvocalized page title (Wiktionary:About_Arabic / Wiktionary:Arabic_entry_guidelines, 'Entry name'), so the scraped input is a consonant-plus-long-vowel skeleton, exactly the pattern independently measured on the bare 'ar' wikipron row (0/17,563 words carry a haraka there; see ar.json audit.wikipron). No fold was run for this dialect row -- doing so needs the dialect's own vowel inventory, not MSA's -- so no valid_ceiling is recorded here; the wikipron_ar_diacritized loader (scripts/benchmark.py) that would supply it is wired for the 'ar' row only.
